SPECIFICATION FOR ELECTRIC SOLDERING lRONS ( Third Revision )
1 SCOPE 8 MARKING 8.1 Clause

This standard covers general, safety and performance requirement for soldering irons for use in household premises, for connection to supplies at voltagas not exceeding 25OV ac single phase, or dc. In addition to soldering irons having the heating element energized from the mains supply, requirements for soldering irons having the heating element energized at extra low voltage from a step down transformer incorporated in or external to the appliance and intermittently rated soldering irons actuated by push switches It also covers are included in this specification. aspirated or de-soldering irons for removing solder from joints.

9.1 The soldering irons shall comply with the requirements given in clauses 8 to 32 of IS 302-2-45 ( 1994 ).
10 FINISH 10.1 All metal parts of the soldering irons (other than the tip ) shall preferably be constructed of corrosion resisting material to prevent oxidation or injury for soldering flux and fumes. Copper, nickel and chromium electroplated coatings may be used to provide the protection. Copper, nickel and chromium electroplated coating shall conform to the requirements as given tn IS 4827 : 1983. 11 PERFORMANCE 11.1 The tip temperature ( the temperature on the working surface of the tip when the iron is idle ) shall stabilize within the temperature range 300 to 350�C. In addition the time necessary for the temperature of the soldering iron tip to exceed the ambient temperature by 180�C shall be less than 7 minutes.

The soldering iron with either a fine-wire thermocouple attached to the tip or other suitable temperature measuring device attached shall be energised with rated input. Throughout the test, the soldering iron shall be supported by its handle horizontally in free air. The time necessary for temperature of the soldering iron tip to exceed the ambient temperature of 180�C shall be noted and it shall not exceed the value

IS 959 : 1994 When the tip temperature has specified above. become stabilized, the temperature shall be range measured and it shall be within the specified above. 12 ENDURANCE 12.1 The soldering iron shall be connected to the supply and operated under conditions of adequate heat discharge such that the input is 1'15 times the maximum rated input which shall be maintained throughout the test. During the operating period, the tip temperature shall be maintained between 300�C and 35O"C, if necessary by forced cooling. The soldering iron is operated for 96 hours under those condition. 12.1.1 After the test of 12.1, the soldering shall withstand the electric strength test in 16.4 of IS 302-l ( 1979 ). 13 TESTS 13.1 Type Tests The tests specified in Table ; shall constitute the type tests and shall be carried out on two samples of soldering irons of the same type and rating selected preferably at random from a regular production lot. Before cotimencement of the tests, the soldering iron shall be visually examined and inspected for obvious visual defects in respect of components, parts and their assembly, markings, construction, mechanical hazards, provision of suitable terminals for supply connections, earthing and the effectiveness of screws and connections. The external surface finish shall be even and free from finishing defects. 13.1.1 Criteria of Acceptance iron given
